findings.evidence: Bullets at lines 70-72 vs. statements at lines 268-272, 304-308, 338-354. `transvectionWeylElement` is `[[0,1],[-1,0]]` on the `(i,j)` block, so `w² ` is `diag(-1,-1)` there and `diagGL_mul_transvectionUnit_mul_inv` (line 68 bullet) gives `w x_{ik}(c) w⁻¹ = w² x_{jk}(c) w⁻² = x_{jk}(-c)`.
findings.fix: State that `w` moves the index `j` to `i` with the parameter unchanged, that moving `i` to `j` is done by conjugating with `w⁻¹` (hence the `_inv_conj_` variants), and list those two lemmas in the bullet.
findings.issue: The added bullet says conjugation by a transvection Weyl element "exchanges the corresponding index of another transvection", implying index exchange is always parameter-free. Only the `j → i` direction is: `w x_{ik}(c) w⁻¹ = x_{jk}(-c)`. The bullet also omits `transvectionWeylElement_inv` and `transvectionWeylElement_inv_conj_transvectionUnit_left`/`_right`, which are the lemmas actually consumed by `Symplectic/Weyl.lean`.

findings.evidence: Module docstring lines 18-44 unchanged apart from the two bullets; new section at lines 247-354.
findings.fix: Add a sentence to the prose: the file also builds `n_{ij} = xᵢⱼ(1) xⱼᵢ(-1) xᵢⱼ(1)`, the representative of the transposition in `N(T)`, and records how conjugation by it moves the indices of the other transvections — the `N`-half of the data pinning the elementary matrices against the torus.
findings.issue: The header prose (lines 21-44) still describes the file as the commutator relations plus torus conjugation only, and states that the `xᵢⱼ(c)` against `xⱼᵢ(d)` case "is deliberately absent" — but the PR adds a `## Weyl elements` section (def + 5 theorems) built from exactly that pair. The prose never says what this material is or why it lives here.

summary: The new declarations are individually documented and the symplectic module docstring is accurate, but the updated Transvection.lean module header both under-describes the new Weyl material and summarises the conjugation lemmas in a way that promises more than they deliver (the parameter is unchanged only in the stated direction; the opposite direction negates it).
